title: Civil Engineering Technologists and Technicians
description: Apply theory and principles of civil engineering in planning, designing, and overseeing construction and maintenance of structures and facilities under the direction of engineering staff or physical scientists.

tasks.text: Inspect project site and evaluate contractor work to detect design malfunctions and ensure conformance to design specifications and applicable codes.
Conduct materials test and analysis, using tools and equipment and applying engineering knowledge.
Draft detailed dimensional drawings and design layouts for projects to ensure conformance to specifications.
Analyze proposed site factors and design maps, graphs, tracings, and diagrams to illustrate findings.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Develop plans and estimate costs for installation of systems, utilization of facilities, or construction of structures.
Plan and conduct field surveys to locate new sites and analyze details of project sites.
Calculate dimensions, square footage, profile and component specifications, and material quantities, using calculator or computer.
Read and review project blueprints and structural specifications to determine dimensions of structure or system and material requirements.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with supervisor to determine project details such as plan preparation, acceptance testing, and evaluation of field conditions.
Prepare reports and document project activities and data.
Develop project budgets by estimating the cost of project activities.
Respond to public suggestions and complaints.
Negotiate with contractors on prices for new contracts or modifications to existing contracts.
Report maintenance problems occurring at project site to supervisor and negotiate changes to resolve system conflicts.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Autodesk Land Desktop, Autodesk Revit.

skills.name: Geographic information system
skills.def: Software to capture, manage, analyze, or display geographically-referenced information. Examples: ESRI ArcGIS software, Geographic information system GIS software, Geographic information system GIS systems.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Microsoft Visual Basic, National Instruments LabVIEW.
